# softcats

```{=html}
<div class="pkgdown-hide">
<img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="139"
     alt="softcats logo" />
</div>
```

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/mtkurbucz/softcats/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/mtkurbucz/softcats/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

Regression on predicted categories with calibrated class probabilities.

Many analyses need the association between an outcome and a group that is not
recorded: an ethnic group inferred from names and places, a cell type assigned
by an annotation model, a household type predicted from administrative data. A
classifier gives each observation the probability of each group. The usual
next step, assigning the most likely group or thresholding the probabilities
and regressing on the labels, distorts the estimate (for two groups it
typically attenuates it) and can give confidence intervals whose coverage is
far below the nominal level.

softcats estimates the group differences from the calibrated probabilities
themselves. It partials the controls out of the outcome and the probabilities
with cross-fitted machine learning, solves a Neyman-orthogonal moment
equation, and reports robust standard errors, with survey weights and
clustered designs supported. Diagnostics check the conditions the estimate
needs.

## Installation

```r
# From CRAN
install.packages("softcats")

# Development version from GitHub
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("mtkurbucz/softcats")
```

softcats requires R 4.1 or later and the packages generics and ranger.

## Example

Simulated data with three groups, `A` (the reference), `B` and `C`, whose true
effects are 1 and -0.5:

```{r example}
library(softcats)

d <- sim_softcats(n = 3000, K = 3, seed = 1)

fit <- soft_lm(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3,
               probs = c("prob_A", "prob_B", "prob_C"),
               data = d, seed = 1)
fit
```

Regressions on the most likely labels attenuate the effect of `B`, and their
intervals miss the true value:

```{r hard}
hard <- compare_hard(fit)
hard$estimates[, c("method", "term", "estimate", "conf.low", "conf.high")]
```

The diagnostics run on the subsample in which the group is observed:

```{r check}
soft_check(fit, labelled = d[d$labelled, ], group = "group", extra = ~ z)
```

The [Get started](https://mtkurbucz.github.io/softcats/articles/softcats.html)
article walks through the method, the diagnostics and recalibration.

## Functions

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `soft_lm()` | Group differences from class probabilities |
| `lrn_ranger()`, `lrn_lm()`, `lrn_glmnet()`, `lrn_custom()` | Learners for the nuisance functions |
| `score_spectrum()` | Information in the probabilities beyond the controls |
| `calibration_check()` | Calibration, and calibration given the controls, on labelled data |
| `recalibrate()` | Recalibration on labelled data, checked out of fold |
| `exclusion_test()` | Direct effects of classifier features on the outcome |
| `drift_sensitivity()` | Bias bound under calibration error and robustness values |
| `compare_hard()` | Distortion and implied coverage of regressions on predicted labels |
| `kappa_curve()` | Attenuation across confidence thresholds (two groups) |
| `soft_check()` | All diagnostics in one graded report |
| `sim_softcats()` | Simulated data with known effects |

Fits have methods for `print()`, `summary()`, `coef()`, `vcov()`, `confint()`,
`nobs()`, `residuals()`, `fitted()`, `formula()`, `update()` and `plot()`, and
`tidy()` and `glance()`, so they work with broom, modelsummary and
`lmtest::coeftest()`.

## Assumptions

The estimand is the partial association between the group and the outcome
given the controls, not a causal effect. It is identified when

1. the probabilities are calibrated given the controls (stronger than the
   marginal calibration of Platt scaling or isotonic regression);
2. the classifier uses features beyond the controls, so that no linear
   combination of the non-reference probabilities is a function of the
   controls;
3. those extra features affect the outcome only through the group.

`calibration_check()`, `score_spectrum()` and `exclusion_test()` check these
conditions. `recalibrate()` repairs the first on labelled data, and
`drift_sensitivity()` shows how much miscalibration the conclusion can
tolerate.
